pair.title: Pair this transmitter
pair.description:
**Pair Home Assistant only once.** Use this only if Home Assistant is not paired yet, for example after **Unpair all remotes**. The panel keeps at most two remotes. Pairing Home Assistant can make the panel drop your other remote. Pairing that remote again afterward keeps both working.

The panel ignores Home Assistant until you pair it.

1. Switch the panel's power off at its light switch or breaker, then on again. The remote's power button does not work for this.
2. Wait until the panel is back on. That can take up to 30 seconds.
3. Tick the box below and select **Submit** straight away. The panel blinks.
4. Pair your other remote again: switch the power off and on, wait until the panel is back on, then hold the remote's power button for 10 seconds until the panel blinks.

data.confirm: The panel just came back on

unpair_all.title: Unpair all remotes
unpair_all.description:
This makes the panel forget **every** remote, Home Assistant included. Afterward, none of them works until you pair it again.

1. Switch the panel's power off at its light switch or breaker, then on again. The remote's power button does not work for this.
2. Wait until the panel is back on. That can take up to 30 seconds.
3. Tick the box below and select **Submit** straight away. The panel blinks.

Then pair Home Assistant again with **Pair this transmitter**, and pair your remote again after that.

data.confirm: Remove every remote. The panel just came back on

abort.unpair_all_sent: Unpairing runs for 10 seconds. When the panel blinks, it has forgotten every remote. Then pair Home Assistant with Pair this transmitter, and then your remote.
